This means you must write custom parsing logic, handle metadata, and mathematically justify your Chunking Strategy (e.g., why 500 tokens with a 50-token overlap? The RAG logic and the Vector Database must be wrapped in a FastAPI backend and containerized using Docker. Your TA must be able to run your entire system using a simple docker-compose up command. Phase 1: Data Processing & Vectorization Formulate a research question/querying problem. Parse your unstructured data, apply your chunking strategy, vectorize the text using an appropriate embedding model, and store it in a Vector Database (e.g., ChromaDB, FAISS, Qdrant). Phase 2: System Architecture (FastAPI & Docker) Build a robust API interface for your RAG logic using FastAPI. You are expected to apply clean software engineering principles (such as the MVC pattern) to separate your routing, your RAG logic, and your data models. Phase 3: The RAG Logic & Retrieval Implement the querying pipeline. Your API must accept a user query, embed it, perform a vector search to retrieve the top-k most relevant chunks, inject those chunks into an LLM context window, and return the generated answer via the API endpoint.Phase 4: Evaluation & Error Analysis RAG systems are prone to hallucination and poor retrieval. You must evaluate your system's Retrieval Accuracy. Present at least 3 edge-case queries where the system failed (e.g., it retrieved the wrong chunk, or the LLM hallucinated despite the context) and explain why the architecture missed the mark. Phase 5: The Technical Report (Documentation) Submit a standalone 1-2 page Markdown or PDF document. This is your "Tech Spec." It must include an Executive Summary, a system architecture diagram, your API documentation (endpoints and expected JSON payloads), a justification of your embedding model and chunking strategy, and clear Docker deployment instructions.
